info.title: Permguard stream common
info.description: Components shared by the decision and event evidence surfaces: the stream block, its coverage, signer spans, Merkle inclusion paths and the retention refusal. Declares no paths.

Coverage.description: What a block proves about what it covers: a filtered view cannot claim chain completeness.

contiguous.description: Whether the returned records are a contiguous run of one producer's stream, so the chain links across them.

examined.description: How many positions this read examined to produce the block.

scan_bounded.description: Whether the scan bound stopped the block before its record or byte bound did; the block may be short or empty and `next` has still advanced.

Coverage.x-grpc-note: Shared by two identical protos: permguard.control.v1.ReadCoverage (decisions) and permguard.control.v1.EventCoverage (events), each with contiguous, examined, scan_bounded; each evidence document maps its own `coverage` member to its message.

Step.description: One step of a Merkle inclusion path: a sibling, and which side it is on.

left.description: Whether the sibling sits on the left of the node being carried up.

Step.x-grpc-note: One sibling of an inclusion path, carried inside the JSON bytes of an element of `inclusion` (permguard.control.v1.ReadResponse, permguard.control.v1.ListRecordsResponse).

Inclusion.description: One record's place in the Merkle tree its batch was signed with.

leaf.description: The digest of the record, which is the leaf.

root.description: The root the path reaches: the one the signed envelope attests.

path.description: The siblings, from the leaf upwards.

Inclusion.x-grpc-note: Carried as JSON bytes: one element of `repeated bytes inclusion` in permguard.control.v1.ReadResponse and permguard.control.v1.ListRecordsResponse.

SignerSpan.description: One stretch of a stream and the key that signed it: it covers `[from, next span's from)`.

from.description: The first offset this key signed.

kid.description: The name the batch signatures carry.

jwk.description: the public key, closed: a member a public JWK does not carry, a private `d` included, is refused

SignerSpan.x-grpc-note: Shared by three similar protos (permguard.control.v1.DecisionSignerSpan, permguard.control.v1.SignerSpan, permguard.data.v1.TemporalSignerSpan) that differ from this schema: REST names the first offset `from`, gRPC `from_seq`, and REST carries `jwk` as a JSON object while gRPC carries it as `bytes` holding the JWK's JSON text.

Signers.description: The signer manifest of one stream, as kept in `signers.json`: every signing-key change in offset order.
Signers.x-grpc-note: The on-disk `signers.json` manifest of one stream; no gRPC message carries it as such (the signer RPCs answer with typed spans plus the acked frontier).

Frontier.description: How far a read observed, across whatever contributes to its scope. Carried base64url-encoded in `high_watermark` and `until`, not as a JSON member of a response.

covered.description: The exclusive covered position of each contributing producer, by stream key.

Frontier.x-grpc-note: Part of the opaque, authenticated offset: gRPC carries the offset as the string fields `from`/`next`/`until`, never as a structure.

Position.description: Where a consumer stands inside one segmented stream. Lives only inside an authenticated offset token.

segment.description: The first sequence of the segment being read.

offset.description: How many records of that segment have been returned.

Position.x-grpc-note: Part of the opaque, authenticated offset: gRPC carries the offset as the string fields `from`/`next`/`until`, never as a structure.

Cursor.description: What an offset token stands for before it is MAC-signed. The token (`next`, `from`) is opaque to a client; this schema documents what the server seals into it.

scope.description: The scope it was issued for.

filters.description: The digest of the normalized filter set it was issued under.

positions.description: Where in each contributing stream the next page begins.

Cursor.x-grpc-note: The decoded content of the opaque offset: gRPC carries the offset as the string fields `from`/`next`/`until` (ReadRequest, ReadResponse, ListRecordsRequest, ListRecordsResponse) and never as a structure.

Block.description: One block of an evidence stream. `records`, `proof` and `inclusion` are open values here; each evidence document restates the block with typed records.

records.description: The records, in the scope's deterministic order.

next.description: The offset to present for the following block: opaque and authenticated, never absent.

oldest_available.description: The oldest offset this scope still holds.

high_watermark.description: The exclusive end this read observed, as the opaque token a client echoes as `until`.

more.description: Whether there is more, relative to the request's `until` when it has one and to `high_watermark` otherwise.

proof.description: The signed envelopes covering these records, when the reader asked.

inclusion.description: One inclusion path per record, when the reader asked.

Block.x-grpc-note: The shared shape of two identical responses, permguard.control.v1.ReadResponse (decisions) and permguard.control.v1.ListRecordsResponse (events); each evidence document restates it (DecisionBlock, EventBlock) and maps its own.

OffsetExpired.description: The 410 body of a consumer that fell behind retention: expected behaviour, not corruption. The refusal envelope plus where to resume.

oldest_available.description: The oldest offset still held, to resume from deliberately.

requested_sequence.description: The sequence the consumer stood at.

OffsetExpired.x-grpc-note: REST 410 body. gRPC answers an expired offset with a status and metadata (class, code) and no message; `oldest_available`, `oldest_sequence` and `requested_sequence` have no gRPC field.
